recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Do not revive the removed 2015 implementation; the current FHIR-19248 Summary/Detail implementation is the maintained form of the same split-table TOC requirement.
issue_request: FHIR-7785 asked to make sections of the long full table of contents expandable or contractible; the final Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution was to split the table into two parts.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied by svn revision 5968, represented in git as 4011bfee6bc94b1671b232b2509c735ed17d94f0, which split source/toc.html into Documentation and Resources tabs using <%toc1 Documentation%> and <%toc2 Resources%>. A later 2016 layout commit, 4a631751a530a015bb8bca5cdf6c1de93f165448, removed that old tab split and restored a single <%toc%> include.
additional_context: FHIR-19248 later addressed the same FHIR-core-toc manageability problem and refined the maintained current-spec split as Summary and Detail tabs. Commit 7eeb9d5742ff32958ce43681cf30b2475d5ca48a is already on the combined branch and implements that Summary/Detail split in active source/toc.html. publish.ini lists toc.html as an active special page. Zulip and Confluence searches found no FHIR-7785-specific evidence that conflicts with this conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active current TOC source already has a Summary tab that filters the generated table to the second level and a Detail tab that preserves the full generated table, satisfying FHIR-7785's resolved intent without restoring the obsolete 2015 Documentation/Resources jQuery UI implementation.
